dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals finally convicted of specific pandemic loan/grant fraud and any small businesses tied to them as owners, officers, or key employees.
dimensions.evidence: An associate of a small business concern who is finally convicted of any crime involving or relating to financial misconduct or a false statement with respect to a covered loan or grant shall be ineligible

dimensions.assessment: Bars targeted individuals and associated small businesses from obtaining SBA financial assistance, altering their eligibility status completely.
dimensions.evidence: ineligible to receive any financial assistance from the Administrator, other than financial assistance under section 7(b).

dimensions.assessment: Prevents the allocation of certain future SBA financial assistance funds to disqualified parties, with no specific monetary totals provided.
Amends Section 16 of the Small Business Act to add explicit disqualification criteria for financial assistance.
dimensions.evidence: Section 16 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 645) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory prohibition on future SBA assistance for convicted parties, with prospective application.
dimensions.evidence: shall not apply to any contract or other agreement entered into by the Government prior to the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The exact count of individuals or businesses impacted by these conviction criteria is not stated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill prohibits individuals finally convicted of financial misconduct or false statements concerning specific COVID-19 pandemic loans and grants, as well as their associated small businesses, from receiving Small Business Administration financial assistance, excluding disaster loans.
